narrative.intro: Techflow recorded $310M in contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Techflow won 3 awards so far, with an average award size of $103M, and obligations are up 26.6% year over year. The Department of Homeland Security is the dominant buyer, accounting for $310M of obligations. Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance is Techflow's largest market at $310M, with smaller work in Custom Computer Programming Services at $347K and Security Guards and Patrol Services at $5K. Fiscal-year history shows obligations of $193M in FY21, $247M in FY22, $223M in FY23, $271M in FY24, $245M in FY25, and $310M in FY26. These figures are partial for the current fiscal year and represent contract obligations and award-value totals where noted. The picture is of a concentrated buyer base and market profile, with one agency and one NAICS category accounting for the bulk of obligations.

sections.heading: How concentrated are Techflow's federal obligations?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security accounts for $310M of Techflow obligations in FY2026 to date. Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance accounts for $310M of Techflow obligations, showing a high concentration in one agency and one market. The General Services Administration accounts for $347K, and two smaller markets account for $347K and $5K respectively, indicating most spend is clustered.

sections.heading: How has Techflow's obligation trend evolved recently?
sections.body: Techflow's obligations rose to $310M in FY26 from $245M in FY25 and $271M in FY24. Earlier years show obligations of $223M in FY23, $247M in FY22, and $193M in FY21. Overall, obligations are up 26.6% year over year for the current fiscal-year-to-date period.

faq.a: Techflow has $310M in contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Techflow won 3 awards so far in the period, with an average award size of $103M, and obligations are up 26.6% year over year.
